name: Red-capped Robin
rangeDescription: Interior of southern australia, to southern and western coasts
description: Small Australian robin. Male black above, with a black head and chin, vivid scarlet breast and forecrown.

name: Zimmer's Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of southern bolivia (chuquisaca and tarija) and northwestern argentina (jujuy and salta)
description: Distinctive tapaculo of humid montane forest adjacent to treeline and Polylepis forest in the high Andes in NW Argentina and S Bolivia. Striking white throat distinctive from other tapaculos except White-browed, from which it differs by voice and gray (not brown) hind crown.

name: Red-breasted Merganser
rangeDescription: Breeds southern greenland, iceland, northern british isles, and scandinavia to sakhalin and kamchatka peninsulas, and kuril and commander islands (southeastern russia), in south through northern kazakhstan and northeastern china; western alaska mainland through mainland canada from arctic to northern great lakes and eastward to nova scotia; winters to coasts of southern europe, black and caspian seas; japan, korean peninsula, and eastern china; to west-central mexico, gulf coast, and florida
description: Long-bodied duck with a thin bill and shaggy crest. Breeding males have a dark green head, brown breast, and gray sides.

name: Golden Palm Weaver
rangeDescription: Savanna of ethiopia to southern somalia, eastern kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: Breeding male is bright yellow with a mostly orange head. The female is duller, though still very yellow.

name: Southern Red Bishop
rangeDescription: Western and southern angola, southern and eastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, kenya, and tanzania, southward to south africa
description: A small, dumpy sparrow-like weaver. The breeding male is a mix of velvety vermilion and black; the narrow black forecrown is diagnostic.

name: Socotra Buzzard
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: A typical medium-sized brown-and-white buzzard that was only recognized as distinct in 2010. The underparts are whitish buff with heavily streaked underparts (lighter on the throat).

name: Chilean Flamingo
rangeDescription: Andes of southern south america; pampas of southern brazil to southern argentina
description: Widespread and often numerous; found at shallow lakes and lagoons from the high Andes to Patagonian steppe and even in coastal waters. Adult is distinctive: pale pink with a salmon-pink “bustle” and grayish legs with red feet and “knees.” Immature often obviously smaller than adult, but has longer bill “hook” than the smaller and shorter-legged James’s Flamingo.

name: Chestnut-shouldered Goshawk
rangeDescription: Montane forest of northern and eastern new guinea
description: A very rare and little known, powerful raptor of foothill and lower montane forest interior. Black crown, dark wings with chestnut edged shoulders, heavily streaked chest and barred belly.

name: Little Stint
rangeDescription: Northern palearctic; winters to africa and indian subcontinent
description: Tiny shorebird with extensive range across Europe, Africa, and Asia. Very rare vagrant in North America.

name: Sedge Warbler
rangeDescription: Palearctic region; winters to southern africa
description: Small, well-marked warbler. Most striking plumage features are the contrasting broad, pale buffy eyebrow and dark crown stripes; otherwise, upperparts rich dark brownish overall (with indistinct streaking), underparts buffy.

name: Glossy Flowerpiercer
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to western venezuela, ecuador and far northern peru
description: This glossy-black flowerpiercer has a distinctive silvery patch on the shoulder. Most similar to Black Flowerpiercer, which is smaller and lacks the shoulder patch in most of its range (although in east Andes in Colombia, Black Flowerpiercer has a small gray shoulder patch).

name: Leyte Plumed-Warbler
rangeDescription: East-central philippines (leyte and samar)
description: A tiny and very little-known bird of foothill forest on Samar and Leyte islands. Yellow below, with a broad yellow eyebrow and olive upperparts.

name: Yellow-winged Tanager
rangeDescription: Eastern mexico to eastern nicaragua
description: Fairly common in tropical lowlands and foothills, favoring forest edge and woodland, as well as semi-open areas such as towns and gardens with larger trees. Mainly feeds at mid-upper levels in trees, eating fruit, and perches readily on phone wires.

name: Stripe-breasted Starthroat
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (pernambuco to bahia, goiás, and são paulo)
description: A large hummingbird found in forest and semiopen habitats such as savannas. Males have a green body bisected by a white stripe on the belly.

name: Scarlet-breasted Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Southern vietnam, malay peninsula, sumatra, riau and lingga archipelagos, and borneo
description: The bright scarlet-red chest of the otherwise bumblebee-colored male glows in the gloom of the forest like a demon’s eye. Female is much more modestly-colored, with a gray head, a yellow breast, whitish flanks, and a dull brownish-yellow back.

name: Saddle-billed Stork
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa
description: A tall, lanky, black-and-white stork with a unique red, yellow, and black bill. The male has dark-brown eyes, and the female has yellow eyes.

name: Gray-crowned Crocias
rangeDescription: Vietnam (langbian plateau)
description: Resembles a three-way cross of a shrike, a sibia, and a laughingthrush. Black robber’s-mask, warm orange-brown back, streaked white underparts, and long gray tail with white tips below.

name: Little Stint
rangeDescription: Northern palearctic; winters to africa and indian subcontinent
description: Tiny shorebird with extensive range across Europe, Africa, and Asia. Very rare vagrant in North America.

name: African River Martin
rangeDescription: Large rivers of democratic republic of the congo; winters to coastal gabon
description: Enigmatic and distinctive, this compact all-dark martin has striking red eyes and a bright orange-red bill. Juvenile is duller.

name: Swainson's Hawk
rangeDescription: Western north america; winters to northern argentina, southern brazil, and paraguay
description: Longer-winged than Red-tailed Hawk, but otherwise the same size. Found in prairies and agricultural regions of western U.S.
